cover.hook: 3 ways your AI agent gets turned against you.
cover.sub: From the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, with the fix for each.

slides.title: 1. Goal hijack (ASI01)
slides.body: Instructions hidden in a web page, email or file the agent reads redirect what it's trying to do. Fix: keep instructions separate from content, scan inputs, and check the goal before the agent acts.

slides.title: 2. Tool misuse (ASI02)
slides.body: The agent calls a connected tool in a way nobody intended, by mistake or because an attacker steered it. Fix: authorise every tool call, validate parameters against a schema, scope each tool.

slides.title: 3. Privilege abuse (ASI03)
slides.body: Overbroad tokens, or sub-agents that inherit all of the parent's permissions. Fix: scoped tokens, on-behalf-of flows, and just-in-time credentials you can revoke.

items.ig_caption:
3 ways your AI agent gets turned against you. 🤖

From the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (Dec 2025):
→ Goal hijack (ASI01): instructions hidden in content the agent reads redirect its goals. Fix: separate instructions from content and check the goal before acting
→ Tool misuse (ASI02): the agent uses a connected tool in a way nobody intended. Fix: authorise each tool call and validate its parameters
→ Privilege abuse (ASI03): overbroad tokens, sub-agents inheriting full permissions. Fix: scoped, just-in-time credentials you can revoke

Do this week: list every tool each agent can call, swap shared tokens for scoped ones, and treat web pages, emails and files as untrusted input.
